# Names and rights

Last updated: 2026-11-08.

This is an English translation. The [Japanese version](./names.md) governs; if the two differ, the Japanese version applies.

## Where the names come from

- **Nusquama**: a name formed from the Latin adverb nusquam ("nowhere"). In a letter to Erasmus dated 3 September 1516, Thomas More called the work later known as Utopia "Nusquama". The earlier wording is in the [King's errata](../ERRATA.en.md).
- **Nemo**: Latin for "no one".
- **Mukau (無何有)**: an old word for a place where nothing is, from the "land of nothing whatever" in the Zhuangzi.
- **Rex Eques (Knight-King)**: a word joining knight and king.

All of these come from common words or classics; none borrows the name of a particular work, body or person.
Nusquama has no relation to Utopia, Twenty Thousand Leagues Under the Seas, works on the Arthurian legend, or their characters, pictures or coats of arms.

## The emblem

The emblem was drawn by the operator with rectangles and polygons only.
It does not copy the arms or insignia of any real state, royal house, order of knighthood, decoration, university or company.

## Licence

The text and the emblem of Nusquama are published under CC BY 4.0 ([LICENSE](../LICENSE)).
Anyone may copy, adapt and redistribute them, with attribution.
But CC BY 4.0 neither gives effect to the titles of Nusquama nor allows the emblem to be used as a real insignia.
CC BY 4.0 allows only what copyright covers. It does not reach other rights such as trademarks, or limits set by other laws.
The emblem and the titles must not be used as if they were the insignia of a real body or official titles ([Terms of Use](./terms.en.md)). Such use may, apart from copyright, break the law (such as Article 1, item 15 of Japan's Minor Offenses Act).
The text and the emblem were written with Claude Code at the operator's request. How far copyright reaches in what is made with a language model is not settled. CC BY 4.0 allows only as far as rights reach.

## If you find an infringement of your rights

If you think that any part of Nusquama infringes your rights, let us know as set out in [Requests for removal, correction or withdrawal](./requests.en.md).

---

Source: https://nusquama.vercel.app/policies/legality.en.html

# Legality Statement

Last updated: 2026-11-11.

This is an English translation. The [Japanese version](./legality.md) governs; if the two differ, the Japanese version applies.

## What this page is

This page sets out, law by law, why the operator believes Nusquama breaks no law.
For each law it lists what must be present for the law to apply (the elements) next to the facts of Nusquama, and shows that no fact meets the elements.
It also shows where in the pages the rules that keep those facts true are written.

This page sets out the operator's understanding; it is neither legal advice nor a guarantee.
It has not been reviewed by a lawyer.
The statutes are summarised, not quoted, and the law names are given in common English renderings.
The summaries were checked on 2026-11-08 against the current texts obtained from the e-Gov law API. The articles checked are listed in each heading.
The texts were obtained by querying the e-Gov law API (v1) from GitHub Actions.
The original texts can be read on [e-Gov Laws Search](https://laws.e-gov.go.jp/) (in Japanese).
At the end of each section, under "Text of", the wording itself is quoted.
The Japanese articles are quoted unchanged from the texts obtained from the e-Gov law API and recorded by the watch.
Foreign treaties, laws and explanations are quoted from the texts fetched on 2026-11-11 from the pages that publish them, without translation.
If the law or the facts change, this page will be revised.

## How Nusquama is run

Nusquama means no harm. It does not aim to deceive anyone or to hurt anyone.
The operator runs Nusquama in compliance with the laws of Japan and with the terms of the services it uses.
If the operator learns that something may break a law, the operator stops that part first, then checks it and fixes it.
When it is unclear whether something is lawful, the operator chooses not to do it.
This stance is promised in the [Terms of Use](./terms.en.md), under "No ill intent, and obeying the law".

## The facts relied on

The analysis below rests on the following facts. Each can be checked in the public repository and on the site.

- It has no territory and claims no land.
- It has no people, government, army or police.
- It issues no currency, passports, identity documents or certificates.
- It receives no money or goods. It sells nothing, takes no donations and shows no advertising.
- It makes and hands out no physical decorations, badges or uniforms.
- Its titles are words inside the fiction, used only in the repository, on the site, and in the articles and posts the King wrote to introduce Nusquama (listed in the README under "ほかの場所").
- The only personal information it handles is a GitHub account name, a link to the public correction, and the description the person writes. The linked page may reveal a real name or affiliation, and the form says so.
- It accepts no applications from people under 16, or from people whose country of residence forbids receiving knightly titles conferred by private persons.
- It collects no documents to check nationality, age, country of residence or real name. Age, country of residence and the country the applicant is in when applying are taken from the applicant's own declaration, made by ticking the oaths in the form.
- Every page states that it is fiction and unrelated to anything real.

## Law by law

### Insurrection (Penal Code, Article 77)

- **Elements, in summary**: rioting with the purpose of destroying the governing machinery of the state, excluding state power over its territory and exercising power there, or otherwise subverting the basic constitutional order of government. What counts as a riot (many people joining to use violence or threats to the point of disturbing the peace of a locality) is not in the text; it comes from the usual interpretation.
- **Nusquama's facts**: it has no territory and does not try to exclude the government or power of Japan or any other country. There is no gathering of people, no violence and no threat. Article 9 of the Basic Law says the kingdom draws no sword and settles disputes with words and evidence.
- **Why the law does not apply**: there is neither the purpose nor a riot.
- **Rules that keep this true**: Terms of Use, "What Nusquama is"; Basic Law, Articles 1 and 9.

<!-- 条文 刑法 第77条 -->

### False titles and insignia (Minor Offenses Act, Article 1, item 15)

- **Elements, in summary**: falsely claiming an official post, court rank or decoration, academic degree or other title set by law, or a foreign equivalent of these; or, without the right to do so, using a uniform, decoration, badge or other insignia set by law, or anything made to look like one.
- **Nusquama's facts**: Knight-King and knight are words inside a work of fiction, set by no country's law. Because Nusquama is not a state, its titles are not "foreign equivalents" either. It makes no physical decorations, badges or uniforms, and its emblem imitates no real insignia.
- **Why the law does not apply**: the titles used are not titles set by law, and no physical insignia are used. Using the titles in a way that could be mistaken for a legal title is itself forbidden.
- **Rules that keep this true**: Terms of Use, "Titles" (no use that could be mistaken for a legal title; nothing on CVs, business cards or official documents); Basic Law, Article 8; [Names and rights](./names.en.md), "The emblem".

<!-- 条文 軽犯罪法 第1条第15号 -->

### Official documents and passports (Penal Code, Article 155; Passport Act, Article 23)

- **Elements, in summary**: forging, for use, a document that a public office or public official is to make (Penal Code, Article 155). Using a passport in another person's name, or handing over, receiving or holding a forged passport for use, among others (Passport Act, Article 23).
- **Nusquama's facts**: it makes no passports, identity documents, certificates or letters of appointment. Knighting only adds an account name to the roll and issues no document.
- **Why the law does not apply**: no document that could be forged is made.
- **Rules that keep this true**: Terms of Use, "What Nusquama is" (no passports, no nationality); [Rules on Knighting](./knighting.en.md), "What knighting is" (no documents or objects).

<!-- 条文 刑法 第155条、旅券法 第23条 -->

### Fraud (Penal Code, Article 246)

- **Elements, in summary**: deceiving a person into handing over property, or by that means obtaining an unlawful financial benefit.
- **Nusquama's facts**: it receives no money or goods. It sells no titles, takes no donations, and knighting is free.
- **Why the law does not apply**: no property or benefit changes hands.
- **Rules that keep this true**: Terms of Use, "Fees"; Basic Law, Article 6; the fifth of the ten precepts. The Terms also say that anyone claiming to grant Nusquama's titles for a fee has nothing to do with Nusquama.

<!-- 条文 刑法 第246条 -->

### Trade (Act on Specified Commercial Transactions, Article 2; Act against Unjustifiable Premiums and Misleading Representations, Article 5; Consumer Contract Act, Articles 2, 8 and 10)

- **Elements, in summary**: a seller or service provider selling goods or services door to door, by mail order, by telephone solicitation and so on (Act on Specified Commercial Transactions). A business making representations about its own goods or services that mislead people into thinking they are much better or more favourable than they are (premiums and representations act). In a contract between a consumer and a person acting as a business, a clause that fully excludes the business's liability for damages, among others, is void (Consumer Contract Act).
- **Nusquama's facts**: it sells nothing, shows no advertising and runs no business.
- **Why the law does not apply**: the transactions these laws assume do not exist. In case the Consumer Contract Act ever applies, the "Liability" section of the [Disclaimer](./disclaimer.en.md) says that the exclusion does not apply and that the operator is liable, including for slight negligence. Article 8(1) of that Act voids full exclusions of liability, and Article 8(3) voids partial exclusions that do not make clear they apply only to slight negligence. The Disclaimer falls under neither.
- **Rules that keep this true**: Terms of Use, "Fees".

<!-- 条文 特定商取引法 第2条、景品表示法 第5条、消費者契約法 第2条、消費者契約法 第8条、消費者契約法 第10条 -->

### Currency and means of payment (Payment Services Act, Article 3)

- **Elements, in summary**: issuing prepaid payment instruments, that is, tokens or electronic records issued in return for payment matching an amount or a quantity, which can be used to pay for, or to claim, goods or services.
- **Nusquama's facts**: it issues no currency, points, vouchers or electronic value.
- **Why the law does not apply**: nothing is issued or handled.
- **Rules that keep this true**: Terms of Use, "What Nusquama is" (no currency).

<!-- 条文 資金決済法 第3条 -->

### Trademarks and indications (Trademark Act, Article 25; Unfair Competition Prevention Act, Article 2, paragraph 1, items 1 and 2)

- **Elements, in summary**: using, without right, a registered trademark for the designated goods or services, which the trademark owner has the exclusive right to use (Trademark Act). Using an indication identical or similar to another person's indication of goods or business that is widely known among consumers, causing confusion; or using, as one's own indication, something identical or similar to another person's famous indication (Unfair Competition Prevention Act).
- **Nusquama's facts**: it does no business. Its names come from ordinary Latin words and words from the classics, and borrow no one's indication of goods or organisation. The emblem is the operator's own work.
- **Why the law does not apply**: there is no use in business, and no one else's indication is used.
- **Rules that keep this true**: [Names and rights](./names.en.md); Disclaimer, "Relation to real things".

<!-- 条文 商標法 第25条、不正競争防止法 第2条第1項第1号・第2号 -->

### Copyright (Copyright Act, Articles 21 and 23)

- **Elements, in summary**: reproducing a work, or transmitting it to the public (including making it transmittable), which the author has the exclusive right to do, without permission.
- **Nusquama's facts**: the text and the emblem were written with Claude Code at the operator's request and checked by the operator. No one else's work is copied. Utopia and the Zhuangzi are named only as sources of the names, and none of their text is copied. Both are long out of copyright.
- **Why the law does not apply**: no one else's work is reproduced.
- **Rules that keep this true**: [Names and rights](./names.en.md); [Requests for removal, correction or withdrawal](./requests.en.md) (requests to remove content that infringes a right).

<!-- 条文 著作権法 第21条、著作権法 第23条 -->

### Personal information (Act on the Protection of Personal Information, Articles 17, 18, 27 and 28)

- **Elements, in summary**: a business handling personal information must specify the purpose of use as far as possible and not handle the information beyond what that purpose needs. Before giving personal data to a third party, or to a third party in a foreign country, it must obtain the person's consent, among other rules.
- **Nusquama's facts**: it handles only the GitHub account name, the link to the correction and the description the person writes, and asks for no real name, address or contact details. It states the purpose of use, that the information is public, and that it is handled by GitHub and Vercel in the United States, and the person consents in the application form. Withdrawal from the roll and removal are granted at any time, free of charge.
- **Why the law does not apply**: the handling the law requires is met by the pages and the form.
- **Duty by duty**: the duties of Articles 17, 18, 20–23, 25–28, 32–38 and 40 of the Act, Article 10 of its Cabinet Order and Articles 7, 8, 10 and 17 of its Rules are paired, paragraph by paragraph, with the sentences that meet them, in `verification/duties.json`. The texts were fetched from e-Gov and read on 2026-11-08. The check confirms that every sentence exists and that every article is watched.
- **Rules that keep this true**: [Privacy](./privacy.en.md); [Rules on Knighting](./knighting.en.md), "Withdrawal and revocation"; the pledges in the application form.

<!-- 条文 個人情報保護法 第17条、個人情報保護法 第18条、個人情報保護法 第27条、個人情報保護法 第28条 -->

### Reputation and credit (Penal Code, Articles 230 and 231; Civil Code, Article 709)

- **Elements, in summary**: publicly alleging facts that damage a person's reputation; publicly insulting a person, even without alleging facts; infringing, intentionally or negligently, another person's rights or legally protected interests and so causing damage.
- **Nusquama's facts**: it discusses no particular person. The roll of knights lists only account names, on the person's own application and consent. When an application is refused, the reason is given briefly and the person is not judged.
- **Why the law does not apply**: nothing damages anyone's reputation.
- **What others write**: applicants and people making requests write text in issues. If something that harms another person's reputation or exposes their personal information is written there, the operator takes it down at once, before deciding anything else.
- **Rules that keep this true**: Terms of Use, "What is not allowed" (no defamation or harassment); [Requests for removal, correction or withdrawal](./requests.en.md), "After a request".

<!-- 条文 刑法 第230条、刑法 第231条、民法 第709条 -->

### Status under international law

- **Elements, in summary**: under international law, a state is generally expected to have a permanent population, a defined territory, a government, and the capacity to enter into relations with other states (Montevideo Convention of 1933, Article 1). Article 3 of the same convention says that the political existence of a state is independent of recognition by other states. The convention is among American states, and Japan is not a party to it, but it is widely cited for the criteria of statehood. The text was checked on 2026-11-08 in the [English text of the Avalon Project (Yale Law School)](https://avalon.law.yale.edu/20th_century/intam03.asp), and the parties in the [list of the Organization of American States](https://www.oas.org/juridico/english/sigs/a-40.html), which is the depositary.
- **Nusquama's facts**: it has no population, territory or government, and claims no sovereignty and no land. It claims no state's territory, no land that belongs to no state, and no structure at sea. It enters into no diplomatic relations and seeks no recognition as a state. It issues no passports and no nationality.
- **Why the law does not apply**: it meets none of the four criteria and does not try to. Nusquama is not a state under international law and holds no rights or duties under it. It impairs no state's sovereignty, territorial integrity or status under international law.
- **Rules that keep this true**: Terms of Use, "What Nusquama is"; Disclaimer, "A work of fiction"; Basic Law, Article 1.

<!-- 条文 モンテビデオ条約 第1条、モンテビデオ条約 第3条 -->

### Nationality (Nationality Act, Article 11)

- **Elements, in summary**: a Japanese national who acquires a foreign nationality of their own choice loses Japanese nationality.
- **Nusquama's facts**: Nusquama is not a foreign state and grants no nationality. Knights are not nationals. Knighting only adds an account name to the roll.
- **Why the law does not apply**: there is no "foreign nationality" to acquire, so knighting changes no one's nationality. The same holds under any country's nationality law.
- **Rules that keep this true**: Terms of Use, "What Nusquama is" (no nationality); [Rules on Knighting](./knighting.en.md), "What is not checked" (no nationality granted).

<!-- 条文 国籍法 第11条 -->

### Laws outside Japan

- Nusquama is a non-profit work of fiction run from Japan. It does no business and no trade in any country, and solicits no money and no paid membership.
- Some countries forbid falsely claiming their honours or titles. Nusquama forbids using its titles outside the kingdom and any use that could be mistaken for a real title or honour (Basic Law, Article 8; Terms of Use, "Titles").
- For example, Article 8 of Italian Law No. 178 of 1951 forbids private persons and bodies from conferring knightly distinctions under any name. The same article also punishes anyone who uses such a distinction, and applies even when it was conferred abroad. The text was checked on 2026-11-08 in [Normattiva](https://www.normattiva.it/uri-res/N2Ls?urn:nir:stato:legge:1951-03-03;178~art8), Italy's official database of legislation. Applications from people living in such countries are not accepted ([Rules on Knighting](./knighting.en.md), "Who may apply"). The country of residence is taken from the applicant's own declaration and is not checked ([Rules on Knighting](./knighting.en.md), "What is not checked").
- The EU General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) can reach those outside the EU, for example when they offer services to people in the EU. In case it does, Nusquama handles only what the person makes public themselves, takes it with consent, and answers requests for access, correction and erasure free of charge ([Privacy](./privacy.en.md)). Article 3(2) of the GDPR applies to a controller outside the EU where it offers goods or services, irrespective of payment, to people in the EU, among other cases. The text was checked on 2026-11-08 in [EUR-Lex](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX:32016R0679).
- The California Consumer Privacy Act (CCPA) covers businesses run for profit. Nusquama runs no business for profit, so the operator considers that it does not apply. This was checked on 2026-11-08 on the [CCPA page of the California Attorney General](https://oag.ca.gov/privacy/ccpa), which says the Act covers for-profit businesses and generally does not apply to nonprofit organisations. The page of the statute itself blocks automated access, and was not read.
- The operator has not checked the laws of other countries one by one.
- From 2026-11-22, only people who live in Japan and are in Japan when they apply may apply, whatever their nationality. The laws of other countries cannot all be checked, so people who live where one of them might reach are not accepted at all. Some of those laws reach people who are in the country, not only those who live there, so an application made while abroad, for travel, work or study, is not accepted either ([Rules on Knighting](./knighting.en.md), "Who may apply").
- The applicant's declaration is not checked, but if the linked correction states clearly that the applicant lives outside Japan, is outside Japan when applying, or is under 16, the operator asks the applicant, and does not knight them unless they are confirmed to meet the conditions. This keeps what could have been noticed from being overlooked ([Rules on Knighting](./knighting.en.md), "What the operator checks").

<!-- 条文 イタリア 1951 年法律第178号 第8条、GDPR 第3条第2項、CCPA 司法長官の説明 -->

### The terms of the services used

- **GitHub**: the repository and issues are used in line with GitHub's terms. Nothing they forbid is placed there.
- **Vercel**: the site is served on Vercel's Hobby plan, which is limited to personal, non-commercial use (Vercel's [Fair Use Guidelines](https://vercel.com/docs/limits/fair-use-guidelines), checked on 2026-11-08). Nusquama is non-commercial and meets that condition.

<!-- 条文 Vercel Fair Use Guidelines -->

## Acts outside the rules that come near a law's elements

Nusquama itself is set up so that, for every law above, it has no fact that meets the elements.
But if a knight, a reader or a third party acts against the rules, or outside them, that person's act may come near a law's elements.
The table lists such acts, the laws they come near, and the operator's caution.
It lists possible paths. It does not say that a listed act is always an offence or unlawful, nor that an act not listed is safe.

| Act | Law it comes near | Caution |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Writing a title on a CV, business card, paper, official document or job title, or presenting it like a real title or honour | Minor Offenses Act, Article 1, item 15 | Do not. The [Terms of Use](./terms.en.md), "Titles", forbid it |
| Using a title outside Japan, or applying while living outside Japan and giving a false country | Laws outside Japan (such as Article 8 of Italy's Law No. 178 of 1951) | Do not. Article 8 of the Basic Law and the [Rules on Knighting](./knighting.en.md) forbid it. Once known, the knighting is withdrawn |
| Selling titles, certificates, insignia or membership in Nusquama's name, or collecting donations or fees | Penal Code, Article 246; Act on Specified Commercial Transactions, Article 2; Act against Unjustifiable Premiums and Misleading Representations, Article 5 | Do not. Nusquama sells nothing and takes no donations ([Terms of Use](./terms.en.md), "Fees"). Anyone who does so has no connection with Nusquama |
| Making a "Nusquama passport", "citizen card" or similar paper, and showing it to prove who one is | Penal Code, Article 155; Passport Act, Article 23 | Do not make or show one. Nusquama has no passports and no nationality. Making it so that it may be taken for a document of a real office or state comes near an offence |
| Putting the emblem or the name "Nusquama" on goods, services or advertising | Trademark Act, Article 25; Unfair Competition Prevention Act, Article 2, paragraph 1, items 1 and 2; Act against Unjustifiable Premiums and Misleading Representations, Article 5 | Do not use them in trade. How they may be used is on the [Names and Rights](./names.en.md) page |
| Making currency, points or vouchers in Nusquama's name and handing them out for a price | Payment Services Act, Article 3 | Do not. Nusquama has no currency |
| Naming and judging another person, or writing another person's personal information, in an issue or elsewhere | Penal Code, Articles 230 and 231; Civil Code, Article 709 | Do not. Such text is removed at once, before any decision |
| Applying under the age of 16 by giving a false age | Civil Code, Article 5 | Do not. Once known, the name is removed from the roll, even without a request |

The responsibility for an act done against the rules, or outside them, lies with the person who did it.
The operator is not responsible for such acts of knights, readers or third parties.
When the operator learns of one, the operator withdraws the knighting, removes the text, or states that it has no connection with Nusquama.
This does not apply where the law makes the operator responsible ([Disclaimer](./disclaimer.en.md), "Liability").
The texts of the laws cited in each section above can be read under that section.

## How this was reviewed, and the risks that remain

The conclusion of this page was checked in the five ways below.

1. **Elements as logic**: an offence or a duty arises only when all of its elements are present. Writing the elements as A₁ ∧ A₂ ∧ … ∧ Aₙ, one fact that denies a single Aᵢ makes the whole false. For each law, `verification/legal-matrix.json` lists which element is denied by which sentence, and the check confirms that the sentence exists.
2. **Coverage**: every pair of actor (operator, applicant, knight, reader, third party) and act (publishing, receiving applications, listing on the roll, using titles, keeping information, reaching abroad) is listed in `verification/legal-matrix.json`. Every pair is either covered by an item on this page or cannot occur.
3. **Consistency**: the pages were compared for the same matter being written differently. The extent of "inside the kingdom" differed from page to page, so it is now defined once, in the Terms of Use, and the other pages point there (the King's errata, entry 6).
4. **Fault tree**: the ways the facts relied on could fail were listed, likelihood and severity were each estimated from 1 to 3, and the product was used to rank them. The numbers are the operator's estimates and serve only to rank.
5. **Breaking on purpose**: each fixed sentence was altered in turn, and the check was seen to fail.

The review is not done once only. Once a week, the articles this page relies on and GitHub's terms are fetched from the e-Gov law API and from GitHub, and compared with the recorded values (`tools/statutes.js`). If they differ, a proposal is made by itself, with the difference between the old and the new text: a pull request, or an issue with a link that opens one in a single step. The operator reads the difference, checks this page, and adds the label 記す; a workflow then runs the checks on the merged result and records the change only if they pass. If a fetch fails, an issue opens. If this page names an article that the watch does not cover, the check fails.

The ways the facts relied on could fail are these.

| No. | How it could fail | Likelihood | Severity | Product | Response |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Someone under 16 applies, lying about their age | 2 | 2 | 4 | Once known, the name is removed from the roll and the issue deleted, without waiting for a request |
| 2 | A promise in the pages is removed or weakened by an edit | 2 | 2 | 4 | `verification/check.js` fails |
| 3 | Someone writes another person's personal information or defamation in an issue | 1 | 3 | 3 | Taken down at once, before deciding anything else |
| 4 | A third party sells titles in Nusquama's name | 1 | 3 | 3 | The Terms of Use say such a person has nothing to do with Nusquama |
| 5 | Someone living in a country that forbids it applies, lying about where they live | 1 | 2 | 2 | Once known, the name is removed from the roll |
| 6 | A knight uses the title outside the kingdom as if it were real | 1 | 2 | 2 | The knighting is revoked |
| 7 | A name overlaps with someone else's registered trademark | 1 | 2 | 2 | Registrations have not been checked; a request is handled through the Requests for Removal, Correction or Withdrawal |
| 8 | A service used changes its terms and can no longer be used | 1 | 1 | 1 | That part is stopped first, then checked |

People aged 16 and 17 are minors under the Japanese Civil Code. An agreement made without the consent of a legal representative can be cancelled. Nusquama receives nothing that it would lose by such a cancellation.

<!-- 条文 民法 第5条 -->

## Conclusion

In the operator's analysis, no fact meets the elements of any of the laws above.
The operator considers the risk of illegality to be very small.
This is not a legal guarantee. If the facts relied on change, so does the conclusion.
The facts relied on are fixed in the pages and the Basic Law.
The repository's check (`verification/check.js`) fails if those sentences are removed.
The same check confirms that the page sections and Basic Law articles this page refers to exist.

Anyone who finds a possible illegality can report it through the [Requests for removal, correction or withdrawal](./requests.en.md). The operator will check it, fix it, and revise this page.

## How the agreement on courts works

The Terms of Use put settlement by agreement first, and then name an agreed court of first instance. This section says how far that clause reaches.

- **The law, in summary**: the parties may, by agreement, choose the court of first instance. The agreement has no effect unless it concerns claims arising from a defined legal relationship and is made in writing or as an electronic record (Code of Civil Procedure, Article 11). An agreement on which country's courts will hear future disputes over a consumer contract has effect only in limited cases, such as when it allows claims in the courts of the country where the consumer lives (Code of Civil Procedure, Article 3-7, paragraph 5).
- **Nusquama's facts**: people applying for knighting tick their agreement to the Terms of Use in the form, and the tick stays in the issue. People who only read the site or the repository tick nothing.
- **How it works**: with those who agreed in the form, a record of the agreement remains as an electronic record. With those who only read, there is no written agreement, so the agreement on courts may have no effect. In that case, the court set by law has jurisdiction. The Terms state that they do not take away the right of a consumer, or of a person outside Japan, to sue in another court where the law allows it.
- **Rules that keep this true**: Terms of Use, "Governing law and disputes"; the pledges in the application form.

<!-- 条文 民事訴訟法 第11条、民事訴訟法 第3条の7 -->

Source: https://nusquama.vercel.app/policies/exchange.en.html

# Rules on exchange

Last updated: 2026-11-10.

This is an English translation. The [Japanese version](./exchange.md) governs; if the two differ, the Japanese version applies.

## About these rules

These rules set out how Nusquama deals with other micronations (self-declared states) and fictional countries.
Nusquama is a work of fiction, not a state. Exchange, too, takes place within the fiction.

## How exchange takes place

- Exchange is limited to greetings and links to each other's pages.
- No treaty, alliance or document of mutual recognition is concluded, so that no promise looks like a relation between states.
- No title, decoration or rank is conferred on each other. The only thing Nusquama gives is knighthood under the Rules on Knighting.
- No exchange involves money, goods or services.
- There is no exchange with anything that claims to be a real state, royal house or order of knighthood, that sells titles, or that deceives people.
- The other party, too, is respected as a work of its own, and Nusquama neither accepts nor denies the claims of its country.

## How it is decided and ended

The King decides whether to engage in an exchange.
When an exchange begins, a link to the other party's page is put, with the date, under "Elsewhere" on the top page.
Either side may end an exchange at any time. When it ends, the link is taken down, and the day is kept in the timeline.

## Requests

The operator of the other country may ask for a link to be corrected or taken down, by the procedure in [Requests for removal, correction or withdrawal](./requests.en.md).

---

Source: https://nusquama.vercel.app/founding.en.html

# Founding Declaration, Basic Law and Ten Precepts

Last updated: 2026-11-11.

This is an English translation of three parts of the top page. The [Japanese version](./README.md) governs; if the two differ, the Japanese version applies.

## The founding declaration

The declaration is a dated text, and it is not rewritten (Ten Precepts, II).
The King's errata correct two of its statements, in entries 1 and 3 of [the King's errata](./ERRATA.en.md).

There is a country that is nowhere.
Its name is Nusquama: in Latin, "a place that is nowhere". It is the name that Thomas More first nearly gave to the island that later became Utopia.

The country that is nowhere has a king who is no one.
The King's name is Nemo: in Latin, "no one".
The Knight-King Nemo I has no subjects. The one person the King rules is the King alone.

This King does not wield a sword.
The King's weapon is the check, and the King's shield is the errata.
The King's greatness is not measured by how few errors there are. It is measured by the honesty of a record that keeps its errors instead of erasing them.

The crown lasts one reign, and has no heir.
For only those who stand alone can correct themselves alone.

Here the founding of the Knightly Kingdom of Nusquama (Regnum Nusquamae) is declared.

Nemo I, the Knight-King, 7 November 2026

## The Basic Law of the Kingdom

**Article 1 (Fiction)** This country is a work of fiction. It is not related to any real state, royal house, order of knighthood, honour or title, and it has no territory, people, currency or passports.

**Article 2 (The King)** The King is one person only, Nemo I, the Knight-King (Nemo I, Rex Eques Nusquamae). The reign lasts one generation and is not inherited.

**Article 3 (The domain)** The domain of the Kingdom is the King's bookshelf and the errata that the King has made public. The domain widens each time the King admits an error.

**Article 4 (The King's vows)** The King does not silently withdraw a vow once made. When the King amends a vow, the King leaves a record of what was replaced by what.

**Article 5 (The King's errors)** The King does not erase the King's own errors, and records them with a date. An erased error counts as a second error.

**Article 6 (Knighting)** Knighting is free of charge. It is not given in exchange for money, goods or services. It has one condition: to have publicly corrected one of one's own errors.

**Article 7 (The Order)** Knights belong to the Order of Errata (Ordo Erratorum). There is one rank only, "knight", with none higher or lower.

**Article 8 (Where the titles are used)** The titles of this country are used only within this country. They are not written in a CV, a paper, on a business card, in an official document or in any academic setting.

**Article 9 (Arms)** The Kingdom does not draw its sword. Disputes are settled by words and evidence.

**Article 10 (Amendment)** The King amends this Basic Law. Articles 1, 6 and 8, however, are never removed.

## The Ten Precepts of the Knight-King

I. Do not fill a gap with a guess. What you do not know, write that you do not know.

II. Do not rewrite frozen words. To correct them, write on a separate sheet.

III. If you speak of numbers, speak in a form that can be counted again.

IV. Do not adorn yourself with titles. The name of the Knight-King is allowed only within this country.

V. Take no money. A rank bought is no rank.

VI. Do not erase errors. Errors are the King's domain.

VII. One thing to a sentence. A sword, too, makes one cut to a stroke.

VIII. Do not raise your voice. Show severity by how much you cut away.

IX. Do not be ashamed of being alone. Only those who stand alone can correct themselves alone.

X. Put the King, too, to the check.

Source: https://nusquama.vercel.app/knights.en.html

# Roll of the Order of Errata (Ordo Erratorum)

> This is a work of fiction, written for fun. The titles of those named here have no legal effect and no real honour.

This is an English translation. The [Japanese version](KNIGHTS.md) governs; if the two differ, the Japanese version applies.

The knights are listed in the order of their knighting. There is only one rank, "knight", with nothing above or below it (Basic Law, Article 7).
Names are given as GitHub account names, with no real name or affiliation.
A knight may ask at any time to be taken off the roll ([Rules on Knighting](policies/knighting.en.md)).

| No. | Knight | Knighted | Mistake corrected | Application |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |

Nemo I, Knight-King, is the King and is not on this roll.

---

Source: https://nusquama.vercel.app/errata.en.html

# The King's errata

> This is a work of fiction, written for fun. In these errata the King within the fiction records the King's own mistakes.

This is an English translation. The [Japanese version](ERRATA.md) governs; if the two differ, the Japanese version applies. The quotations below are translated from the Japanese.

Under Article 5 of the Basic Law, the King does not erase the King's own mistakes, and records them with a date.
The Founding Declaration is a text issued with a date. As a frozen text it is not rewritten; its mistakes are recorded here (Precept 2).
The text of the rules may be changed. When text is replaced or removed, the text before the change is kept here.
These errata are the domain under Article 3 of the Basic Law.

| No. | Recorded | Where | Wrong | Right | Checked against | Category | Place name |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | 2026-11-08 | Founding Declaration | "the name Thomas More first nearly gave to the island that later became Utopia." | In a letter to Erasmus dated 3 September 1516, More called the work "Nusquama". The King has found no source showing that it was nearly the name of the island. | John Michael Parrish, "A New Source for More's 'Utopia'", The Historical Journal (1997) ([Cambridge Core](https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/historical-journal/article/new-source-for-mores-utopia/47DF9A7A407D4BB379DF6265220CB5B0)) | Fact | Insula Facti I |
| 2 | 2026-11-08 | Names and rights, "Where the names come from" | "the name Thomas More used for the island that later became Utopia." | As in 1. The text of the rules was changed the same day. | As in 1 | Fact | Insula Facti II |
| 3 | 2026-11-08 | Founding Declaration; Names and rights, "Where the names come from" | "Latin for 'a place that is nowhere'." | The Latin nusquam is an adverb meaning "nowhere". Nusquama is More's name formed from it. The text of the rules was changed the same day. | None. The meaning of the word is general knowledge, not checked in a dictionary | Word | Insula Verbi I |
| 4 | 2026-11-08 | Legality Statement, "Facts relied on" | "The titles are used, as words within the fiction, only in the repository and on the site." | The King wrote an article on MicroWiki himself and uses the titles there too. The sentence was changed to "only in the repository, on the site, and in the article on MicroWiki that the King wrote himself". | The King's article (README, "ほかの場所" (Elsewhere)) | Scope | Insula Finis I |
| 5 | 2026-11-08 | Disclaimer, "Liability" | "The operator is not liable, to the extent permitted by law, for loss arising from use of the site or the repository." | "To the extent permitted by law" is a partial exclusion that does not make clear it is limited to slight negligence, and may be void under Article 8(3) of the Consumer Contract Act. It was changed to exclude liability except for intent or gross negligence, and not to apply where that Act applies. | Article 8 of the Consumer Contract Act (text obtained through the e-Gov Laws API) | Law | Insula Legis I |
| 6 | 2026-11-08 | Rules on Knighting, "Withdrawal and revocation"; Legality Statement, "Laws outside Japan" | "when a title is used outside this kingdom (the repository and the site)" | The King also uses the titles in the MicroWiki article (4), which did not fit the scope in brackets. What "within this kingdom" means was set in one place, "Titles" in the Terms of Use, and the other pages were changed to point there. | The Legality Statement, "Facts relied on", and entry 4 of these errata | Scope | Insula Finis II |
| 7 | 2026-11-08 | Terms of Use, "Titles"; Legality Statement, "Facts relied on" | "an article the operator wrote himself to introduce this country" (Terms of Use); "only in the article on MicroWiki that the King wrote himself" (Legality Statement) | Not a mistake; the scope was changed. As the King also announced the founding on X, calling himself Nemo I, Knight-King, it became "articles or posts" written by himself to introduce it, each listed under "ほかの場所" (Elsewhere) in the README. | The King's post (README, "ほかの場所" (Elsewhere)) | Scope | Insula Finis III |
| 8 | 2026-11-08 | Legality Statement, "Standing in international law" | "Recognition by other states also bears on whether something is treated as a state. The text of the convention was not checked; this rests on general knowledge." | Placed right after the convention was named, it read as if the convention said so. Article 3 of the convention says the opposite: the political existence of a state is independent of recognition by other states. Article 3 is now quoted as it is, with where the text of the convention and its parties were checked. | Montevideo Convention ([English text at the Avalon Project](https://avalon.law.yale.edu/20th_century/intam03.asp), [list of parties at the Organization of American States](https://www.oas.org/juridico/english/sigs/a-40.html)) | Law | Insula Legis II |
| 9 | 2026-11-08 | Terms of Use, "Who these terms cover" | "Using the site or the repository means accepting these terms." | There is no agreement with those who only read, and standard terms reach only those who agreed or were told beforehand that the terms would form part of a contract (Civil Code, Article 548-2). Consent is now taken in the application form, and reading is not treated as consent. For readers, the law sets what each side owes. | Article 548-2 of the Civil Code | Law | Insula Legis III |
| 10 | 2026-11-11 | The King's errata; the timeline; README, "ほかの場所" (Elsewhere) | "X: the post announcing the founding (listed under "ほかの場所" in the README)." (the Wrong of the deleted row) | On 2026-11-08 the link to the post on X was taken out of "ほかの場所" in the README, and this was recorded as the earlier entry 9 and as a row of the timeline. On the same day both rows were deleted, and the later entries were renumbered (the present entry 9 is a different row). The deleted entry said that this was not a mistake but a change of scope, and that the post is not inside the kingdom. Deleting a recorded row is a second mistake against Article 5 of the Basic Law. Entry 7 says that the post on X was also to be listed under "ほかの場所", but it is no longer listed. | The history of the repository (commits 3aa7340 and a7332ca) | Scope | Insula Finis IV |
| 11 | 2026-11-11 | Rules on Knighting, "Who may apply" and "What is declined"; Legality Statement, "Laws outside Japan" | "People who live outside Japan may not apply, whatever their nationality" / "A person who lives in Japan may not apply while outside Japan" (Rules on Knighting, "Who may apply"); "the conditions (age or country of residence)" (Rules on Knighting, "What is declined"); "if the linked correction states clearly that the applicant lives outside Japan or is under 16" (Legality Statement) | Applications are limited to people who live in Japan and are in Japan only from 2026-11-22, but two sentences of the Rules on Knighting gave no date and read as if already in force. "From 2026-11-22" was put at the head of both. Two other places that list the conditions left out the country where the applicant is when applying, which was added. | The sentence beginning "From 2026-11-22, only people who live in Japan" in the Rules on Knighting, "Who may apply", and the notice in the Terms of Use, "Changes and ending" | Scope | Insula Finis V |

The article on MicroWiki (Japanese edition) has the same mistakes as 1 to 3. The article is not rewritten; these errata correct it (Precept 2).

## How entries are recorded

Each entry gives the number, the date recorded, where, the wrong text, the right text, what it was checked against, the category and the place name.

- The numbers run from 1 without gaps.
- The date is the day the King admitted the mistake and recorded it.
- "Where" is the page and section of the text that was wrong.
- "Wrong" copies the wrong text as it was.
- "Right" says what is right and how the text was changed.
- "Checked against" names the source used to confirm the right text. When nothing was checked, it says so (Precept 1).
- The category and the place name follow the rule under "Categories and place names" below.

## What is recorded

The King's errata record only mistakes in the King's own texts.
Mistakes in other people's texts are not recorded. Making someone else's mistake into territory would be judging that person.
If an entry itself turns out to be wrong, the earlier row is not erased. A new row records that the earlier row was wrong ([Institutions](INSTITUTIONS.en.md), "Pardon").

## Categories and place names

Mistakes are sorted into six categories.
The map uses only the three colours of the emblem, so the categories are told apart by the shape of the parcel.

| Category | Shape on the map | Name of the isle |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Fact | square | Insula Facti |
| Word | diamond | Insula Verbi |
| Law | triangle | Insula Legis |
| Scope | hexagon | Insula Finis |
| Typo | wide rectangle | Insula Litterae |
| Number | pentagon | Insula Numeri |

A place name is the name of the isle followed by a Roman numeral for its order within the category (for example, Insula Facti I).
The King does not name places by hand. Once the category is fixed, so is the name.
The name of each isle is the Latin insula ("isle") followed by the genitive of a noun for the category. Their forms come from general knowledge and have not been checked in a dictionary.

## Map

<!-- map -->

Each parcel links to its entry.
The image of the map is [territory.svg](site/territory.svg). Like the text and the emblem, it is under CC BY 4.0 and may be used as it is.

## The oldest parcel

The oldest parcel is entry 1, Insula Facti I.
It was recorded on 2026-11-08, about a sentence in the Founding Declaration.
A mistake about the origin of the kingdom's own name became its first territory.
This parcel will never leave the errata.

# Symbols of the kingdom

> This is a work of fiction, written for fun. None of the symbols here is the flag or insignia of any real state, royal house, order of knighthood or honour, and none stands in for one.

This is an English translation. The [Japanese version](SYMBOLS.md) governs; if the two differ, the Japanese version applies.

The symbols of the kingdom are the emblem, the flag and the map of the domain. Like the emblem, each is drawn with rectangles and polygons only. They use no typeface, so they look the same on every device.

## The flag

![The flag of Nusquama (fiction)](assets/flag.svg)

- A navy field with a gold border, the colours of the shield of the emblem.
- A golden-ratio rectangle in the middle, the same form as the upper half of the emblem.
- Three cornerstones above the rectangle.

It does not take the form of bands side by side or one above the other, so that it is not mistaken for the flag of a real country.

## The map of the domain

![The map of the domain (fiction)](site/territory.svg)

Under Article 3 of the Basic Law, the domain is the King's bookshelf and the errata the King has made public.
The three pillars in the middle of the map are the King's bookshelf. The gold parcels around them are the mistakes recorded in the [King's errata](ERRATA.en.md).
Each mistake recorded adds one parcel. The map is drawn from the errata, not by hand.

## How the flag is drawn

The flag is drawn 900 wide and 600 high (3:2). The numbers are the coordinates of the [flag image](assets/flag.svg) as they are.

1. Fill the field with navy.
2. Draw a gold border 8 thick, 24 in from the edge.
3. Draw a golden rectangle 534 wide and 330 high in light-gold lines 6 thick, with its top-left corner at (183, 155).
4. Cut squares out of the rectangle one by one. Their sides shrink by the golden ratio: 330, 204, 126, 77.9, 48.1, 29.8.
5. Above the rectangle, set three gold squares (the cornerstones) with sides of 24, 12 apart, their top edge at 99.

## How the flag is flown

- The flag is flown only on screens. The King makes no flags of cloth or paper.
- It is not set beside the flag of a real country so as to look like one of them.
- The flag and the map of the domain, like the text and the emblem, are under CC BY 4.0. The rules for their use are in [Names and rights](policies/names.en.md).

## Colours

| Name | Colour code | Where it is used |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Navy | `#14213d` | the field of the shield and of the flag, the sea of the map |
| Gold | `#c9a227` | borders, cornerstones, the parcels of the map |
| Light gold | `#e8cf74` | the golden rectangle, the sword, the bookshelf on the map |
| Deep navy | `#0b1428` | the groove of the sword in the emblem |

The flag and the map of the domain use only navy, gold and light gold.

## Typeface

The symbols use no typeface, so that they look the same on every device.
The text of the pages is shown in a Mincho typeface already on the reader's device (Hiragino Mincho, Yu Mincho and Noto Serif JP, in that order). No font files are served.

## The sign of the kingdom

When the kingdom is shown by a character alone, ∅ (the empty set sign, U+2205) is used, because the kingdom is nowhere.
Emoji are not used, because their shape changes from device to device.

## Creature and flower of the kingdom

- Creature: the snail, because it leaves a trail where it has been, as the King leaves the trail of the King's own mistakes.
- Flower: the forget-me-not, so that mistakes are not forgotten.

Both are defined in words, not drawn. A drawing would make them more likely to be mistaken for real insignia.

## Time and units

- The time of the kingdom is Japan Standard Time. The date changes at the same moment.
- The size of the domain is counted in errata: one entry in the King's errata is one erratum.

## Words of the anthem

There is no music; only the words are given. No one is required to sing them.

- I. On a sea that is nowhere / the King's bookshelf, three pillars / each time a mistake is admitted / the island grows by one.
- II. The sword is not drawn and points down / the shield keeps dates and words / an erased mistake is a second mistake / a mistake not erased is our land.
- III. One king who is no one / rules himself and corrects himself / one rank, the knight / no money taken, only names recorded.

## Trade marks

The operator will not apply to register the kingdom's name, emblem or flag as a trade mark, so that no one holds the symbols alone.

## What is not made

As the [Terms of Use](policies/terms.en.md) say, Nusquama makes and hands out no objects such as decorations, insignia, uniforms or certificates.
No insignia or certificate is given to knights either. Knighting only puts an account name on the [roll of knights](KNIGHTS.en.md) ([Rules on Knighting](policies/knighting.en.md)).

---

Source: https://nusquama.vercel.app/calendar.en.html

# Calendar and days of the kingdom

> This is a work of fiction, written for fun. The days here are anniversaries within the fiction. They are not real public holidays, and they give no one a holiday or a duty.

This is an English translation. The [Japanese version](CALENDAR.md) governs; if the two differ, the Japanese version applies.

The calendar of Nusquama uses the same dates as the calendar of Japan.

| Day | Name | Origin |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 7 November | Founding Day | On this day in 2026, Nemo I, Knight-King, declared the founding |
| 8 November | Day of Errata | On this day in 2026, the King's errata were opened and the first mistake recorded |

On these days the King reads again the King's own mistakes admitted that year.
No knight, and no one else, is required to do anything.

## Importing the calendar

The days are also served as an [iCalendar file](site/calendar.ics). Imported into a calendar app, it shows the days every year.
They come in as all-day days that do not block time, and each says that it is an anniversary within the fiction and not a real public holiday.

## Spending the days

These are suggestions from the King, not rules.

- Founding Day: read the Founding Declaration and the Ten Precepts again.
- Day of Errata: read one of your own texts again. If you find a mistake, correct it with a date.

## Adding a day

Days are added by the King ([Institutions](INSTITUTIONS.en.md), "How decisions are made").

- Only days on which something happened in this kingdom are added.
- Real public holidays and the birthdays or death days of real people are not made days of the kingdom.
- When a day is added, a row is added to this table and to the timeline, so that it appears in the gazette.
- Adding a day gives no one a holiday or a duty.

# Gazette

> This is a work of fiction, written for fun. This gazette lists the proclamations of the King within the fiction. It is not a real official gazette.

This is an English translation. The [Japanese version](GAZETTE.md) governs; if the two differ, the Japanese version applies.

The events of the kingdom are listed newest first.
They come from the timeline on the top page, the [King's errata](ERRATA.en.md) and the [roll of knights](KNIGHTS.en.md). The gazette is made from them, not written by hand.
New entries can also be read in the feed (gazette.xml).

# The story of the founding

> This is a work of fiction, written for fun. The story here is how the kingdom within the fiction came to be. It does not tell of real events or people.

This is an English translation. The [Japanese version](STORY.md) governs; if the two differ, the Japanese version applies.

This story retells the [Founding Declaration and the Basic Law](founding.en.md) in plain words. Where they differ, the Declaration and the Basic Law apply.

## How the kingdom that is nowhere began

A king was counting the mistakes in the texts he had written.
A mistake that is erased can no longer be seen.
But an erased mistake becomes a second mistake (Article 5 of the Basic Law).
The king decided not to erase his mistakes, and to line them up with dates.
The mistakes he lined up formed a small island around his bookshelf.

When he tried to name the island, the king noticed something.
This kingdom is nowhere. He owns no land that appears on any map.
So he named the kingdom Nusquama, a name made from the Latin nusquam ("nowhere").
He named himself Nemo, Latin for "no one".

On 7 November 2026 the king declared the founding.
The next day he recorded his first mistake in the errata. It was a mistake about where the kingdom's name came from.
And so the kingdom's first territory was a mistake about its own name.

## Why mistakes are the domain

A mistake hidden as a shame will happen again.
A mistake kept as a record spares the next reader from stumbling at the same place.
So this kingdom takes pride not in how few mistakes it makes, but in how honestly it keeps the record (Founding Declaration).
The domain grows because the king has made that many mistakes.
It also grows because he has corrected that many.

## What comes next

The king will make more mistakes.
Each time, he adds a row to the [King's errata](ERRATA.en.md) and the domain grows by one parcel.
Anyone who has publicly corrected one of their own mistakes can join the [Ordo Erratorum](KNIGHTS.en.md).

---

Source: https://nusquama.vercel.app/lexicon.en.html

# Words of the kingdom

> This is a work of fiction, written for fun. The words here are used within the fictional kingdom. They are not terms of any real state or organisation.

This is an English translation. The [Japanese version](LEXICON.md) governs; if the two differ, the Japanese version applies.

## Vocabulary

These are the Latin words used in the names and institutions of the kingdom.
Their meanings come from general knowledge and have not been checked in a dictionary (Precept 1).
The Japanese page also gives a reading in kana, as a rough guide to the classical pronunciation.
If a mistake is found, it is recorded in the [King's errata](ERRATA.en.md).

| Word | Reading | Meaning | Where it is used |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| nusquam | nus-quam | nowhere (adverb) | source of the kingdom's name |
| Nusquama | nus-qua-ma | a name made from nusquam | the kingdom's name |
| nemo | ne-mo | no one | the King's name |
| rex | rex | king | the King's title (Rex Eques) |
| eques | e-ques | knight | the title of the King and of knights |
| regnum | reg-num | kingdom | the kingdom's name (Regnum Nusquamae) |
| ordo | or-do | order, rank | the order's name (Ordo Erratorum) |
| erratum | er-ra-tum | mistake | the errata, the order's name |
| errata | er-ra-ta | mistakes (plural of erratum) | the errata |
| primus | pri-mus | first | Nemo I |
| insula | in-su-la | island | place names |
| factum | fac-tum | fact, a thing done | the isle of the category Fact |
| verbum | ver-bum | word | the isle of the category Word |
| lex | lex | law | the isle of the category Law |
| finis | fi-nis | boundary, end | the isle of the category Scope |
| littera | lit-te-ra | letter | the isle of the category Typo |
| numerus | nu-me-rus | number | the isle of the category Number |
| servo | ser-vo | keep, guard | the motto |
| rego | re-go | rule | the motto |
| ipse | ip-se | self | the motto (me ipsum) |
| gladius | gla-di-us | sword | the sword of the emblem |
| scutum | scu-tum | shield | the shield of the emblem |

## The Founding Declaration in Latin

This is the [Founding Declaration](founding.en.md) put into Latin by the King.
The Japanese declaration governs; this is the King's own composition. If a grammatical mistake is found, it is recorded in the King's errata.
Two sentences of the declaration are not carried over: the one on Thomas More and the one stating what the name means. Both contain mistakes, as entries 1 and 3 of the [King's errata](ERRATA.en.md) record.

Est regnum quod nusquam est. Nomen ei Nusquama.

In regno quod nusquam est, rex est qui nemo est. Nomen ei Nemo.

Rex Eques Nemo Primus populum non habet. Unum tantum regit, se ipsum.

Hic rex gladium non stringit. Arma regis probationes sunt; scutum eius tabula errorum est.

Magnitudo regis non paucitate errorum aestimatur, sed fide tabularum quae errores non delent.

Regnum uno rege finitur; heres non constituitur. Solus enim qui solus stat se ipsum solus corrigere potest.

Hic Regnum Nusquamae conditum esse declaro.

Nemo I, Rex Eques, die VII mensis Novembris anno MMXXVI.

# Institutions

> This is a work of fiction, written for fun. The institutions here are rules of the kingdom within the fiction. They are not the bodies or procedures of any real state, and they have no legal effect on anyone.

This is an English translation. The [Japanese version](INSTITUTIONS.md) governs; if the two differ, the Japanese version applies.

This page arranges the [Basic Law](founding.en.md) and the rules by how the kingdom works. Where they differ, the Basic Law and the rules apply.

## Bodies

| Body | Role | Held by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| The King | Changes the Basic Law and the rules, dubs knights, records mistakes | Nemo I, Knight-King |
| Ordo Erratorum | The knights. It has no duties | The knights on the [roll](KNIGHTS.en.md) |
| The King's errata | Records the King's mistakes. Also the domain | The King |
| Gazette | Announces events, with issue numbers | Made automatically from the timeline, the errata and the roll |
| Checks | Confirm that no commitment in the rules has gone | The check code in the repository |

All the bodies are held by the King alone.
Besides the King there are no officials, no assembly and no court.
The part of the King is played by the operator.

## Proclamations and their numbers

Events of the kingdom appear in the [Gazette](GAZETTE.en.md) with an issue number. Issues are numbered from 1, oldest first.
The number of a proclamation is the number of the gazette issue that carries it. For example, the proclamation that laid down the Basic Law and the Ten Precepts is gazette No. 1.

A proclamation is written as one row of the timeline on the top page, in this form:

- Date: the date in Japan time.
- Event: one sentence on what was laid down or done.
- English: the English translation of the event.

Errata and knightings reach the gazette from the rows of the errata and the roll. They are not written in the timeline.

## Population and how people are called

The population is the number of knights of the Ordo Erratorum.
The current population and the numbers by year are in the tables of [For anyone introducing Nusquama](PRESS.en.md). The tables are counted from the roll, not written by hand.
Knights are not citizens. Nusquama gives no nationality ([Rules on Knighting](policies/knighting.en.md)).
Anyone who is not a knight is called a visitor. Visitors have nothing to register or report.
The King is not counted in the population, because the King is not on the roll.

## How decisions are made

The King decides. There are no votes and no elections.
Knights have neither the duty nor the right to take part in decisions. A knight may leave at any time.
The King's decisions are announced in the gazette or by the date of last update of a rule.

## Pardon

Nusquama has no pardon that erases a mistake (Article 5 of the Basic Law).
If a recorded entry itself turns out to be wrong, the earlier row is not erased. A new row records that the earlier row was wrong.
So asking for a pardon makes the domain one parcel larger.
Removing a knight's name from the roll is not a pardon. Leaving and revocation follow the [Rules on Knighting](policies/knighting.en.md).

## Changing the rules

The Basic Law and the rules are changed by the King, in this order:

1. Change the Japanese version, and on the same day the English translation.
2. Change the date of last update of the rule.
3. Where text is replaced or removed, keep the text before the change in the [King's errata](ERRATA.en.md) (as the opening of the errata says).
4. Add a row to the timeline, so that it appears in the gazette.
5. Publish only after the checks pass.

Articles 1, 6 and 8 of the Basic Law are not removed (Article 10).
When a change takes effect and how it is announced follow the [Terms of Use](policies/terms.en.md), "Changes and ending".

## Versions

Nusquama does not number the versions of its rules. A rule is referred to by its date.
Earlier rules can be read in the history of the public repository.

## The yearly review

Every year on 7 November (Founding Day), a review issue opens automatically. The King follows it and checks that the rules and practice still agree.

- Does every page say that this is fiction?
- Is there no way to buy a title or to give a donation?
- Has no knight's request to leave been left unanswered?
- Is the watch on the laws still running?
- Is the English translation up to date with the Japanese version?
- Is the kingdom still unconnected with the operator's other activities?

## Freezing

If the King can no longer keep the kingdom going, the kingdom is frozen. When it is frozen:

- No requests for knighthood are accepted.
- The roll, the errata and the rules stay public as they are.
- Requests for deletion, correction or leaving are answered as far as possible.

The freezing is announced by putting the "Closing words" below on the top page.

## Dissolution

To close the kingdom, the King follows this order:

1. Close the form for requesting knighthood.
2. Put up the closing words and announce them in the gazette.
3. Tell the knights that they may ask to leave the roll, and do so for any who ask.
4. Allow at least 30 days for such requests before stopping the site.
5. Keep the repository, in a read-only state.

Personal data is handled as the [Privacy](policies/privacy.en.md) page says.

## Closing words

This is the draft of the text put up on freezing or dissolution. It is issued with the date of that day.

The kingdom that is nowhere returns to nowhere.
The King's errata stay here. The mistakes are left behind, not erased.
Knights, thank you for correcting mistakes with us.

## Ten years ahead

Some things will not grow, even in ten years.

- No land, currency, passports, certificates or objects will be made.
- No ranks will be added. There is only one: knight.
- Requests from people who live outside Japan, or who are outside Japan when applying, will not be accepted until the laws of that country have been checked.

Some things will go on.

- Recording mistakes and widening the domain.
- Keeping the rules in step with changes in the law.
- Reviewing once a year.

On 7 November 2036, this outlook will be compared with what happened, and the result announced in the gazette.

---

Source: https://nusquama.vercel.app/press.en.html

# For anyone introducing Nusquama

> This is a work of fiction, written for fun. Nusquama is not a state, and the titles it gives have no legal effect.

This is an English translation. The [Japanese version](PRESS.md) governs; if the two differ, the Japanese version applies.

Text and numbers for anyone introducing Nusquama in an article or a post are gathered here.

## Short introductions

- In a phrase: a kingdom that is nowhere, whose territory is its mistakes.
- In a sentence: The Knightly Kingdom of Nusquama is a playful fiction whose domain grows each time its king records one of the King's own mistakes in the errata.
- In a paragraph: Nusquama is a fictional kingdom named from the Latin nusquam ("nowhere"). Its only king, Nemo I, Knight-King, records the King's own mistakes with dates and never erases them. The number of recorded mistakes is the kingdom's domain. Anyone who has publicly corrected one of their own mistakes can be put on the roll of knights, free of charge. The titles have no legal effect, and no money changes hands.

## Sentences to add

An introduction carries these two passages.

This is a work of fiction, written for fun. Nusquama is not a state, and the titles it gives have no legal effect.

Nusquama is a playful fiction. It has no connection with the operator's other activities.

## Census by year

The population is the number of knights on the roll at the end of the year. Knights who have left are not counted.

<!-- census -->

## Template for Founding Day

For use every year on 7 November. Fill in each ○ with the numbers in the tables above.

Today, 7 November, is Founding Day of the Knightly Kingdom of Nusquama (an anniversary within the fiction). In the ○ years since the founding, the King's errata have grown to ○ mistakes and the order to ○ knights. This is a work of fiction, written for fun.

## Template for a greeting

A greeting to the operator of another country, following the [Rules on exchange](policies/exchange.en.md).

To the operator of ○○: this is Nemo I, Knight-King of Nusquama. Nusquama is a fictional kingdom, and its exchanges are limited to greetings and links to each other's pages. It makes no treaties, gives no titles in exchange, and handles no money. If you agree, we would like to place links to each other's pages.

## Name and symbols

The origin of the name and the use of the emblem and the flag are described in [Names and rights](policies/names.en.md) and [Symbols](SYMBOLS.en.md).

# Play

> This is a work of fiction, written for fun. The template and the questions on this page are play within the fiction. Answering them earns nothing.

This is an English translation. The [Japanese version](PLAY.md) governs; if the two differ, the Japanese version applies.

## A template for your own errata

A template for putting errata in your own document.
The table of this template may be used freely without attribution (it is offered under CC0 1.0).
There is no need to mention Nusquama or show its emblem.

| No. | Recorded | Where | Wrong | Right | Checked against |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | 2026-01-01 | Section 2 | (the wrong text, as it was) | (the right text, and how it was changed) | (the source checked; if none, say so) |

Three rules go with it.

1. Do not erase a row. When something is changed, keep the text before the change.
2. Give a date.
3. Say so when something has not been checked.

A mistake corrected in such a table can be used in a request for knighthood ([Rules on Knighting](policies/knighting.en.md)).

## Practice: find the mistake

Each of these five sentences contains one mistake. The answers are under "Answers to the practice" below.

1. A week has eight days.
2. At a pressure of one atmosphere, water boils at about 50 °C.
3. The angles of a triangle in a plane add up to 360 degrees.
4. There are no speling mistakes in this sentence.
5. The knights of Nusquama have three ranks.

## Answers to the practice

1. A week has seven days. Category: Number.
2. About 100 °C. Category: Fact.
3. 180 degrees. Category: Number.
4. "Spelling". Category: Typo.
5. There is only one rank, knight (Article 7 of the Basic Law). Category: Fact.

## Questions on the institutions

1. How many kings does Nusquama have?
2. What is the condition for becoming a knight?
3. How much does knighthood cost?
4. What is the domain made of?
5. How many ranks do knights have?
6. May the title be written on a CV?
7. Which way does the sword of the emblem point?
8. Which articles may not be removed by amendment?
9. On which day is the Day of Errata?
10. On the map, which category is a triangular parcel?

## Answers to the questions

1. One: Nemo I, Knight-King (Article 2 of the Basic Law).
2. Having publicly corrected one of one's own mistakes (Article 6).
3. Nothing. Knighthood is free (Article 6).
4. The King's bookshelf and the errata the King has made public (Article 3).
5. One: knight (Article 7).
6. No. The title is used only within the kingdom (Article 8).
7. Down, for the sword that is not drawn (Article 9).
8. Articles 1, 6 and 8 (Article 10).
9. 8 November ([Calendar](CALENDAR.en.md)).
10. Law ([King's errata](ERRATA.en.md), "Categories and place names").
